title: Rust: Data Types
description: Explore Rust's primitive data types: integers, floats, booleans, characters, and tuples.

steps.title: Integer Types
steps.description: Declare variables for different integer types: `a: i32 = 42`, `b: u8 = 255`, `c: i64 = -1000`. Print all three.

verification.failureMessage: Declare i32, u8, and i64 variables and print them.

steps.title: Float Types
hints: Rust infers `f64` by default for float literals.

verification.failureMessage: Declare f32 and f64 variables and print them.

steps.title: Boolean Type
steps.description: Declare `is_rust_cool: bool = true` and `is_difficult: bool = false`. Print both with `println!`.
hints: Booleans are used in conditions and assertions.

verification.failureMessage: Declare two bool variables and print them.

steps.title: Character Type
steps.description: Declare a `letter: char = 'R'`, `emoji: char = '🚀'`, and `digit: char = '7'`. Print all three.
hints: `char` uses single quotes, not double quotes.
Rust's `char` is 4 bytes and supports Unicode.
Even emojis are valid chars in Rust!

verification.failureMessage: Declare char variables and print them.

steps.title: Tuple Type
steps.description: Create a tuple `person: (&str, i32, f64) = ("Alice", 30, 5.5)` and print each element using destructuring.
hints: Tuples group values of different types: `let tup = ("Alice", 30, 5.5);`

verification.failureMessage: Create a tuple with 3 elements and print all of them.
